summary_paragraph: Ms. ___ was admitted for worsening wheezing, cough, and shortness of breath after a prolonged course at rehab, where she had been treated for suspected pneumonia without improvement. Evaluation revealed an acute exacerbation of COPD and acute on chronic systolic heart failure, supported by elevated BNP and clinical signs of fluid overload. She was treated with a short course of high-dose prednisone, nebulized albuterol and ipratropium, and a brief increase in lasix dose, which was stopped when renal function and sodium began to decline. A CT scan of the neck and chest showed no evidence of tracheal cancer recurrence but noted new left upper lobe consolidation, which was deemed non-infectious given her clinical improvement. She remained in normal sinus rhythm on amiodarone and metoprolol. Discharge planning included a structured steroid taper, resumption of lasix only if weight exceeded 87kg, and follow-up with pulmonology, oncology in six months, and vascular surgery for planned toe amputations due to gangrene. She was discharged to extended care in stable condition.
